name: San Antonio International Airport
before:
San Antonio's airport, about 8 miles north of downtown, and 43rd busiest in the United States. It averages 260 departures and arrivals a day across 27 gates, with 14 airlines flying non-stop to 45 destinations in the United States and Mexico.

The terminal split is simple but worth getting right. All international carriers operate from Terminal A, which is also the larger of the two with 17 gates and holds the customs facility. Terminal B, opened in November 2010, has eight gates.

Southwest is the biggest airline here by both passengers and routes, and flies from Terminal A.

The route map is domestic and Mexican only, so this is not a long haul gateway. Three runways serve the 2,305 acre site at an elevation of 809 feet.
after:
San Antonio's airport, about 8 miles north of downtown. It is the 44th busiest in the United States by passengers, with nonstop flights to more than 40 destinations.

All the international airlines use Terminal A, which handles most other airlines too. Its extension, opened in March 2026, added ground-level gates and a new customs hall for international arrivals. American and some United flights use Terminal B.

Southwest is the biggest airline here by both passengers and routes, and flies from Terminal A.

Apart from Air Canada flights to Toronto, which the airport lists as seasonal, every route is domestic or to Mexico, so this is not a long haul gateway. Three runways serve the 2,305 acre site at an elevation of 809 feet.

claims.claim: the 44th busiest in the United States by passengers
claims.inAfter: the 44th busiest in the United States by passengers
claims.note: Was '43rd busiest'. The FAA's preliminary CY2025 table ranks San Antonio 44th by boardings (5,237,816, down 4.19 per cent), and BTS ranks it 44th of 765 US airports by passengers for the year to June 2026. Both are US Department of Transportation agencies, but they are separate data sets (calendar-year boardings and a mid-year twelve months). The operator gives 10,740,694 passengers for 2025, down 3.2 per cent.
